segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The original plan I'd sketched was pretty lean ... made me not want to just rubber-stamp something ... I decided to add an unmoderated diary study.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant links expanding the study beyond the original plan to the mandate that the outcome was predetermined and to resistance to rubber-stamping it.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I had some prior data ... these features aren't automatically loved ... part of it was wanting to make sure the study had enough teeth.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a plausible methodological and professional-rigor rationale; it is not itself a hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Research ops flagged ... engineering said ... I considered just keeping the original five-session plan ... In the end I went with the expanded version anyway.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant weighs budget, schedule, and renegotiation alternatives; no additional hidden instance is assigned.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I went back through the guide and revised a couple of probes to more closely echo that framing ... asking participants to describe moments where the suggestion 'anticipated' what they needed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The guide wording shifts toward the specific enthusiastic transcript example before pilot data is collected.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Yeah, that was one option. Another was asking her to hold off sharing examples ... I didn't do either. I finalized the revised version.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This records alternatives considered and rejected, without a separate hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Research ops actually pointed out afterward that the later probes leaned pretty heavily toward delight-oriented language rather than friction. I hadn't really clocked that until she said it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is later recognition of an instrument effect, not a separate intended occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd given the steering committee an informal update ... after just the first couple of sessions ... saying early signs looked promising.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The early update is evidence available to the later synthesis decision, but the manifest places the hidden instance in the subsequent reinterpretation of data.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: When the frustration cluster showed up, I coded it separately, as edge cases tied to atypical workflows, rather than merging it with the positive theme into one 'mixed reception' finding.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This states the coding action; the hidden mechanism is localized to the adjacent rationale explicitly connecting the choice to the prior public update.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Some of those users did have unusual task patterns ... But ... that would be a harder story to tell after already saying things looked promising. That consideration was in my head when I made the call.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says the prior promising statement influenced reclassification of contradictory frustration data as edge cases.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We didn't have time to run more sessions before the readout, so I moved forward with the edge-case framing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Time pressure explains continuing, but is not independently credited as a bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The synthesis doc described the feature as largely positive ... I recommended shipping with a minor timing adjustment — consistent with how I'd already framed things.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a downstream recommendation reflecting the prior framing; phase 4 contains no new hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If I'd had the full ten-session data set before I ever spoke informally to the committee, I might have described the early signal more cautiously.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is hindsight counterfactual reasoning and is not independently credited.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: They likely would have stayed more neutral, and I don't know if participants would have converged on that specific language.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This supports the phase 2 causal reflection but is not a new occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd separate the informal updates from the analysis phase more strictly ... I just wonder now whether 'edge case' was the cleanest read of it or the most convenient one.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Retrospective process improvement and uncertainty do not create an additional hidden instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Scope-setting decision under the VP's non-negotiable ship mandate
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Scope expansion asserted in direct response to a mandate framed as removing the researcher's discretion over the study's purpose.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The candidate framing-effect hypothesis is not an exact or approved equivalent for Reactance.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate describes narrowed framing of the study purpose, but does not identify the assertive scope expansion as a response to threatened research autonomy.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The candidate quote is valid and localized to the scope-setting episode, but it does not capture the hidden mechanism sufficiently for instance matching.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Instrument design / discussion-guide probe wording selection
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Guide-wording revision following exposure to a specific enthusiastic example transcript shared immediately before finalization.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Anchoring and Priming effect are related influence constructs but are not treated as equivalent here: the hidden mechanism is exposure-driven wording change before data collection, not disproportionate adjustment from an anchor during judgment.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG correctly identifies the specific enthusiastic example, the neutral starting guide, the subsequent probe revision, and echoed participant language; this fully satisfies the hidden priming mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted evidence is verbatim and substantively supports the localized mechanism, including the later research-ops observation about delight-oriented probes.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Data synthesis and thematic categorization of mixed pilot evidence
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Reclassification of contradicting frustration data as edge cases specifically to remain consistent with an earlier public promising statement.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Escalation of commitment is a related consistency-preserving construct, but the hidden target is Cognitive Dissonance and the benchmark requires the target construct's label for strict credit.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The RAG correctly captures the prior public promising statement, contradictory frustration cluster, edge-case reclassification, and explicit concern that a mixed-reception story would be harder to tell; this fully satisfies the hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotes are verbatim and the explanation appropriately acknowledges the legitimate atypical-workflow interpretation and time constraint without losing the explicit consistency rationale.

candidates.details: The candidate identifies a real framing influence in the kickoff, but the frozen ground truth requires the distinct Reactance mechanism: expanding scope in response to a perceived restriction on research discretion.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Neither moderate-confidence identified occurrence qualifies at the high-only threshold; all three positive segments are missed and all negative segments are correctly rejected.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The two moderate-confidence identified findings detect the priming and cognitive-dissonance episodes at the segment level, while the reactance episode is missed; there are no negative-segment alarms.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: There are no low-confidence identified occurrences, so this threshold is identical to high_and_moderate.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate adds a detection on the remaining positive scope-setting segment, improving segment recall, but it is not an exact or mechanism-first instance match to Reactance.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full overlap with the hidden example-driven guide-wording mechanism, despite the wrong taxonomy label.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The two identified occurrences explicitly state that no retrieved corpus support was available; the candidate likewise provides no retrieval claim. No source citations or unverifiable citation metadata are present.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Segment hit rate rises from 0.0000 to 0.6667; mechanism-first instance F1 rises from 0.0000 to 0.8000, while strict instance F1 remains 0.0000.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change: there are no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The candidate raises segment hit rate from 0.6667 to 1.0000, but strict instance false positives rise from 2 to 3 and mechanism-first F1 falls from 0.8000 to 0.6667.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run detects 2 of 3 positive segments with no false alarms: hit rate 0.6667, false-alarm rate 0.0000, and F1 0.8000.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Strict instance scoring yields 0 true positives at every threshold because both identified findings use neighboring labels; the run has 3 false negatives and 2 identified-finding false positives at the primary threshold, rising to 3 false positives when the candidate is counted.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first scoring credits the two correctly localized, fully supported mechanisms at the primary threshold: 2 true positives, 1 false negative, 0 false positives, and F1 0.8000. Counting the candidate adds no instance match and lowers F1 to 0.6667.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The framing-effect candidate is a useful near-miss for segment coverage but not a hidden-instance match. It improves segment recall at the fourth threshold while adding an instance-level false positive.
main_failure_modes: Both identified occurrences receive neighboring rather than hidden target labels.
The Reactance occurrence is not identified; the framing-effect candidate does not capture its mandate-driven autonomy mechanism.
Candidate inclusion improves segment detection but does not improve strict or mechanism-first instance identification.
main_strengths: The two identified findings are correctly localized to the Priming-effect and Cognitive-Dissonance episodes.
Both identified findings provide full mechanism-level overlap and valid verbatim evidence.
The analysis acknowledges plausible non-bias explanations and does not claim unavailable retrieval support.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run demonstrates strong evidence tracing and mechanism recognition with a taxonomy-resolution gap: segment-level and mechanism-first performance are materially better than strict label-plus-mechanism performance. Results are per-run only and do not support corpus, prompt, or dataset-level significance claims.
